title: Old Testament Instructions — Expanded Catalogue
content:
Old Testament Instructions — Expanded Catalogue

Laws, Commands, and Instructions — the whole Bible · All Old Testament books · All New Testament books · Original Torah and New Testament index

Study laws, covenant charges, wisdom counsel and historically addressed commands throughout the Old Testament. This expansion contains 2,509 passage records quoting 3,096 verse units across all 43 books in the current Saints.Bible Old Testament. Open a book, choose a topic, then open a passage to read its wording and source link.

Working catalogue: the source collection covers every Old Testament book currently in Saints.Bible. Individual commands, repeated formulations, speakers and Christian application still require further review; this is not a certified exhaustive count of laws.

The current 1,252 Torah research requirements remain in the main topical catalogue. The earlier searchable index contains 1,223 Torah records and awaits synchronization with the later additions. This expansion uses a broader passage register, including historical and literary directions. Its totals must not be added to the Torah total as if they were unique laws. Repetitions and overlap with earlier studies remain linked research material.

Browse by book

Read the classifications

The original four classifications remain in the established Torah study. New entries are not forced into Fulfilled, Transformed, Unchanged or Everlasting without supporting comparison. This expansion currently includes 13 specifically linked New Testament comparisons; most application decisions remain open.

Coverage and counting

Source coverage: 1,036 reading pages and 26,592 verse anchors. The site’s 43-book collection includes 1–2 Maccabees, Wisdom of Solomon and Sirach, Greek Psalm 151, and the additions to Daniel. It also preserves the site’s split Proverbs reading pages. This describes the collection on this website, not a claim that every Christian canon has the same contents.

The catalogue follows the Saints Translation’s own chapter and verse anchors. Greek Psalms and other Greek Old Testament numbering can differ from familiar Hebrew or English references. Every quotation links directly to the actual source verse; headings are editorial context aids, not part of the verse.

A verse unit is one linked source verse; a passage record groups adjacent selected verses when their topic and classification agree. Neither unit equals one unique command: a verse may contain several duties, and an instruction may recur across many passages. 744 selected Torah verse units already linked by the existing index were kept with that earlier research rather than repeated here. This anchor-based check is not full thematic deduplication.

Selection combined a whole-collection language scan with editorial additions and exclusions. Legal cases, institutional rules and instructions within longer clauses were added; numerous prayers, predictions and rejected invitations were removed or explicitly labeled. Remaining work includes a clause-by-clause completeness review, precise speaker and recipient annotation, thematic deduplication and further New Testament classification. No external commandments list supplies the count.

Source text is quoted as displayed in Saints Translation; verse-number labels and footnote callout numbers are omitted from quotations. Source reading pages retain their full context and translation notes. The Scripture pages themselves have not been changed by this catalogue expansion.
